scenario: 系统要存储大量按时间追加的监控指标，查询通常按时间范围和少量标签筛选。
scenario_en: The system stores many append-only monitoring metrics, and queries usually filter by time range and a few tags.
q: 什么时候该选择时间序列数据库（TSDB）？
q_en: When should you choose a time-series database (TSDB)?
options: 只要数据里有 timestamp 字段就必须用 TSDB
当业务核心需求是强事务、多表 join 和复杂外键约束一致性时
当通用数据库在高写入、时间范围查询、保留策略和压缩上出现真实瓶颈时
当核心需求是跨全部 series 做 Top-K 排序时
why: 决定性约束是通用数据库先撑不住高写入、时间范围查询或保留/压缩需求；仅有 timestamp 字段不构成理由。先用 Postgres/DynamoDB 顶，顶不住再上专用系统。
why_en: A time-series database is worth adopting once a general-purpose database genuinely bottlenecks on write volume, time-range queries, or retention, not just because the data happens to have a timestamp.
whenOtherWins: 如果查询核心是跨海量 series 的全局排序或强事务/复杂 join，Postgres/DynamoDB 等通用方案通常更直接。
tradeoff: 专用 TSDB 的写入/压缩优化 vs 通用数据库的事务与关系能力
options_en: Any time your data has a timestamp field, you must use a TSDB.
When the business needs strong transactions, multi-table joins, and complex foreign-key consistency.
When a general-purpose database hits real bottlenecks on high write volume, time-range queries, retention, and compression.
When the core need is Top-K ranking across all series.

termDefinitions.meaning: 时间序列数据库，为高吞吐追加写和按时间范围查询优化的专用数据库。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A TSDB, or time-series database, is purpose-built for high-throughput append writes and time-range queries.

termDefinitions.meaning: 常用开源关系型数据库，强于事务和复杂查询。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Postgres is a popular open-source relational database strong at transactions and complex queries.

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 托管的 NoSQL 键值/文档数据库。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DynamoDB is AWS's managed NoSQL key-value and document database.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在大量数据里找出按某指标排名前 K 名的查询模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Top-K is the query pattern of finding the highest-ranked K results by some metric.

optionExplanations: 只看到数据带时间戳就想上 TSDB 是想当然——大量业务表都有时间戳，但没遇到真正的写入或查询瓶颈就不必换存储。
强事务、多表 join 和复杂外键正是 TSDB 的弱项，这种约束下 Postgres 之类的关系数据库才是更直接的选择。
这才是真正的触发点：写入量、时间范围检索或数据保留/压缩已经让通用方案吃不消，专用存储的优化才划算。
全局 Top-K 排序要跨大量 series 比较排名，这不是 TSDB 按 tag+时间定位数据的强项。
optionExplanations_en: Having a timestamp field alone isn't a reason — plenty of business data carries one without ever hitting a write or query bottleneck.
Strong transactions, multi-table joins, and complex foreign keys are exactly where TSDBs struggle, so a relational database like Postgres fits that constraint better.
This is the actual trigger: once writes, time-range reads, or storage costs start straining a general-purpose store, a purpose-built engine starts paying for itself.
Ranking across every series for a global Top-K is a cross-series sort, not the tag-plus-time lookup a TSDB is built for.

scenario: 云监控系统有 100,000 台服务器，每台每 10 秒上报 5 个指标，约 50,000 点/秒、一天约 43 亿点；原始数据保留 30 天（约 1300 亿点）。当前方案是单机关系库逐行 INSERT，并为每行维护两个 B-tree 索引。
scenario_en: A cloud monitoring system has 100,000 servers, each reporting 5 metrics every 10 seconds — about 50,000 points/s and 4.3 billion points/day — and raw data is kept for 30 days (about 130 billion points). The current design inserts row by row into a single relational database and maintains two B-tree indexes per row.
q: 这个写入量级和保留规模对存储引擎设计意味着什么？
q_en: What does this write rate and retention imply for the storage engine design?
options: 单机关系库逐行写入加两个索引就能长期稳定支撑，不需要改变写入方式
这个量级只影响读延迟，写入可以随意排队，不需要特别设计
索引远超内存后逐行 B-tree 维护会变成随机 I/O，写路径宜改为批量、顺序追加 + 后台合并/压缩（LSM、按时间分块）
只要磁盘足够大，这个量级对存储引擎设计没有实质影响
why: 5 万点/秒靠批量写入单机也可能扛住，真正的问题是保留 30 天约 1300 亿点：B-tree 索引远超内存后，每次逐行插入都要随机读写索引页。顺序追加 + 批量整理（LSM / 按时间分块）把随机写换成顺序写，这正是 TSDB 写路径的设计动机。这是设计建议而非唯一方案（例如分区 + 批量 COPY 的关系库扩展也是一种实现）。
why_en: 50k points/s alone might be absorbed by one machine with batched writes; the real problem is ~130 billion points over 30 days: once B-tree indexes far exceed memory, every row insert does random index-page I/O. Sequential appends with batched reorganization (LSM, time-chunked storage) turn random writes into sequential ones — the motivation behind TSDB write paths. It is a design recommendation, not the only option (e.g. a partitioned relational extension with batched COPY is another implementation).
options_en: A single relational DB with row-by-row inserts and two indexes can support this indefinitely without changing how writes work
Only read latency is affected, so writes can queue freely without special design
Once indexes outgrow memory, per-row B-tree maintenance turns into random I/O, so the write path should move to batched sequential appends with background compaction (LSM, time-chunked storage)
As long as disks are big enough, this scale has no real effect on storage engine design
optionExplanations: 错：逐行插入加两个 B-tree 索引，在 30 天约 1300 亿点的规模下，索引远超内存，维护会变成长期的随机 I/O 瓶颈。
错：写入排队本身也要吃资源，忽略写路径设计等于没看见随机 I/O 和索引维护的代价。
对：保留规模让索引远超内存，逐行维护变随机 I/O；批量、顺序追加加后台合并能把随机写换成顺序写。这是设计建议，不是唯一方案。
错：磁盘再大也救不了随机 I/O 和索引维护的开销，瓶颈在访问模式，不在容量。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: row-by-row inserts with two B-tree indexes over ~130 billion points push indexes far beyond memory, making maintenance a long-run random-I/O bottleneck.
Wrong: queuing writes still consumes resources, so ignoring the write path misses the real cost of random I/O and index upkeep.

Right: the retention scale pushes indexes far beyond memory so per-row maintenance becomes random I/O; batched sequential appends with background compaction turn random writes into sequential ones. It is a design recommendation, not the only option.
Wrong: bigger disks don't fix random I/O or index overhead; the bottleneck is access pattern, not capacity.

q: 把大规模指标按 timestamp、host、metric_name、value 存到一张普通 Postgres 行式表，会先在哪里出问题？
q_en: Where does a normal Postgres row table first break down for large-scale metrics stored as timestamp, host, metric_name, and value?
options: 只要给 host 和 metric_name 分别建索引，就能同时保证写入吞吐和查询延迟
问题只出现在磁盘空间上，不会影响写入吞吐或查询延迟
标签字符串按行重复存储，加上高写入下的索引维护，会同时拖慢写入并膨胀存储
只要把 value 列类型换成 REAL 而不是 DOUBLE PRECISION 就能解决
why: 决定性约束是每行都重复存 host/metric_name 字符串，且高写入下索引维护很重；加索引或换数据类型都治标不治本。
why_en: The real bottleneck is repeated label strings in every row plus heavy index maintenance under high write volume, which indexing alone or a smaller numeric type can't fix.
options_en: Adding separate indexes on host and metric_name alone is enough to guarantee both write throughput and query latency.
The problem only shows up in disk space; it doesn't affect write throughput or query latency.
Repeating label strings in every row plus heavy index maintenance under high write volume slows writes and bloats storage at the same time.
Switching the value column from DOUBLE PRECISION to REAL is enough to fix it.
codeSample:
CREATE TABLE metrics (
  timestamp TIMESTAMP,
  host VARCHAR(255),
  metric_name VARCHAR(255),
  value DOUBLE PRECISION
);
-- 4.3B rows/day → host+metric_name 反复重复
-- 50k writes/s 起步，索引越加写入越慢
optionExplanations: 建索引本身也要维护成本，高写入下反而拖慢写入，不能同时保证吞吐和延迟双赢。
膨胀的不只是磁盘——重复标签和索引维护同样拖慢写入，把问题只归为空间是漏看了写入侧。
对——标签字符串按行反复出现，加上写入密集时索引跟着膨胀，两头一起变慢变大。
换数据类型省的字节有限，治不了标签重复和索引维护这两个真正的瓶颈。
optionExplanations_en: Indexes themselves cost maintenance overhead, so under high write volume they slow writes down rather than guaranteeing both throughput and latency.
It's not just disk bloat — repeated labels and index upkeep also slow writes down, so blaming only space misses the write-side cost.
Right — label strings repeat on every row, and index upkeep grows right along with write volume, so both writes and storage take the hit.
Shrinking the numeric type saves a few bytes at best — it doesn't touch the real bottlenecks of repeated labels and index upkeep.
scenario: 10 万台服务器每 10 秒各上报 5 个指标（约 5 万点/秒），先用一张 Postgres 行式表顶着。
scenario_en: You start with a single Postgres row table for 100k servers reporting 5 metrics every 10 seconds, about 50k points per second.

q: 以下哪些属于时间序列数据库（TSDB）？
q_en: Which of these are time-series databases (TSDBs)?
options: ZooKeeper
InfluxDB
Prometheus
TimescaleDB
why: InfluxDB、Prometheus、TimescaleDB 都是面向时间序列的存储/查询系统；ZooKeeper 是协调服务，管理配置和分布式锁，不是 TSDB。
why_en: InfluxDB, Prometheus, and TimescaleDB are time-series systems, while ZooKeeper is a coordination service for configuration and distributed locks, not a TSDB.
options_en: ZooKeeper
InfluxDB
Prometheus
TimescaleDB

termDefinitions.meaning: 面向时间序列的开源数据库，内置 LSM 风格存储引擎。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: InfluxDB is an open-source database built specifically for time-series storage using an LSM-style engine.

termDefinitions.meaning: 基于 Postgres 扩展实现的时间序列数据库。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TimescaleDB is a time-series database implemented as a Postgres extension.

termDefinitions.meaning: 拉取式监控与时间序列存储系统，常配合告警使用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Prometheus is a pull-based monitoring and time-series system commonly paired with alerting.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分布式协调服务，管理配置、命名和分布式锁，不是时间序列数据库。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ZooKeeper is a distributed coordination service for configuration, naming, and locks, not a time-series database.

optionExplanations: ZooKeeper 干的是分布式协调那一类活儿——配置存取、命名、加锁，不落时间序列点，因此不算 TSDB。
InfluxDB 是专门为时间序列打造的数据库，内置 LSM 风格引擎，是典型 TSDB。
Prometheus 拉取式采集并存储时间序列，常配合告警使用，也是 TSDB。
TimescaleDB 在 Postgres 上做时间序列扩展，同样归为 TSDB 阵营。
optionExplanations_en: ZooKeeper is a coordination service for config, naming, and distributed locks — it doesn't store time-series metrics, so it isn't a TSDB.
InfluxDB is purpose-built for time series with an LSM-style engine underneath — a textbook TSDB.
Prometheus pulls and stores time-series metrics and pairs with alerting — also a TSDB.
TimescaleDB extends Postgres for time-series workloads, so it counts as a TSDB too.
scenario: 要为 5 万点/秒的监控指标选一个专用存储，先把候选组件里不是时序存储的筛掉。
scenario_en: You're picking a purpose-built store for a 50k points/second metrics stream and first need to weed out the candidates that aren't time-series stores.

q: Append-only（只追加写）存储的核心思想是什么？
q_en: What is the core idea of append-only storage?
options: 每次写入都先全表扫描，定位后再原地修改
新数据只追加到文件末尾，不做原地更新
只允许删除旧数据，不允许新增写入
每个指标名单独建一个数据库实例
why: 追加写把昂贵的随机 I/O 转成顺序 I/O，特别适合大量持续写入的指标流。代价是之后需要靠 compaction/index 让读取仍然可接受。
why_en: Append-only storage writes new points at the end of files, turning random writes into fast sequential writes.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  A["Metric point"] --> B["Memory buffer"]
  B --> C["Append segment"]
  C --> D["Compact later"]
options_en: Every write scans the whole table first, finds the row, and updates it in place.
New data is only appended to the end of the file, never updated in place.
You can only delete old data; new writes are rejected.
Each metric name gets its own separate database instance.

termDefinitions.meaning: 只在文件末尾追加新数据，不做原地更新的写入方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Append-only storage always writes new data to the end of a file instead of updating in place.

optionExplanations: 全表扫描是最贵的操作之一，append-only 恰恰是为了避免这种开销，不会反过来要求它。
对，新点只追加到文件末尾，把随机写变成顺序写。
只删不写没法承接持续涌入的指标点，append-only 的意义正是能不断安全地写入。
按指标各开一个数据库是运维灾难，append-only 讲的是单个存储引擎内部的写入方式，不是拆分策略。
optionExplanations_en: A full table scan is one of the most expensive operations — append-only exists to avoid exactly that, not require it.
Right — every new point lands at the tail of the file instead of overwriting old data in place.
Delete-only cannot absorb a continuous stream of incoming points — append-only exists precisely to keep writes safe and ongoing.
Spinning up a separate database per metric is an operational nightmare — append-only describes how one engine writes internally, not a sharding scheme.
scenario: 指标以 5 万点/秒持续写入、几乎不改旧点，磁盘写入模式成了瓶颈。
scenario_en: Metrics stream in at 50k points per second and old points are almost never updated, so the disk write pattern is the bottleneck.

q: 在磁盘 I/O 模式上，append-only 写入相比传统原地更新的优势是什么？
q_en: For disk I/O, what advantage does append-only writing have over traditional in-place updates?
options: 它让每次写入都必须先随机寻址到旧 block 再修改
它省去定位旧数据、读、改、写的步骤，只在文件尾部顺序追加
它保证所有查询都不必再使用任何索引
它只能在纯内存数据库里生效，磁盘数据库用不了
why: 原地更新要先定位旧位置再读改写，产生随机 I/O；append-only 只在文件尾追加，把随机变顺序，代价是空间需要靠后台整理回收。
why_en: In-place updates need to locate, read, modify, and rewrite old data, causing random I/O, while append-only writes sequentially at the end and reclaims space later via background compaction.
tradeoff: 顺序追加换取写入吞吐 vs 原地更新换取即时空间复用
options_en: It forces every write to randomly seek to an old block and modify it first.
It skips locating, reading, modifying, and rewriting old data, appending sequentially at the end of the file instead.
It guarantees every query no longer needs any index.
It only works for pure in-memory databases, not disk-based ones.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对磁盘上分散位置的读写，需要额外寻址开销。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Random I/O reads or writes scattered disk locations and pays extra seek overhead.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按顺序连续读写磁盘位置，没有寻址开销。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Sequential I/O reads or writes contiguous disk locations without seek overhead.

optionExplanations: 这描述的其实是原地更新的行为——先寻址再改，append-only 恰好是要去掉这一步。
对，它省掉定位旧数据再读改写这几步，直接在文件末尾接着写，读写模式从随机变顺序。
顺序写省的是磁盘寻道，不代表查询能跳过索引——定位 series 仍然需要 tag index 或类似结构。
顺序追加对磁盘同样有效，机械盘和 SSD 都能吃到顺序 I/O 的好处，不是内存数据库专属。
optionExplanations_en: That's actually describing in-place updates — seek first, then modify. Append-only exists to remove that step.
Right — it drops the locate/read/modify/rewrite dance and just tacks new data onto the end, converting scattered writes into one sequential stream.
Sequential writes save disk seeks; they do not mean queries can skip indexing — locating a series still needs a tag index or similar.
Sequential append helps disk-based engines too — both spinning disks and SSDs benefit from it, it is not exclusive to in-memory databases.
scenario: 写入端是持续追加的指标流、几乎没有对旧点的更新，且要在机械盘上撑住吞吐。
scenario_en: The write side is a continuous append-only metrics stream with almost no updates to old points, and it has to hold up on spinning disks.

scenario: 为高吞吐指标流选型时，需要判断 7200 rpm 机械硬盘上 4KB 随机写和顺序写的吞吐差异。
scenario_en: When choosing storage for a high-throughput metric stream, you need to judge the throughput gap between 4 KB random writes and sequential writes on a 7200 rpm spinning disk.
q: 机械硬盘上，随机 I/O 相比顺序 I/O 的差异大致是什么量级？
q_en: Roughly how large is the gap between random and sequential I/O on a spinning disk?
options: 随机 I/O 比顺序 I/O 快约 100 倍，写路径不用特意设计
4KB 随机写约 100–200 IOPS（≈ 0.4–0.8MB/s），顺序写约 100–200MB/s，按字节算差两个数量级以上
两者差距在 2 倍以内，寻道延迟可忽略
磁盘 I/O 模式和数据库写入路径的设计无关
why: 机械硬盘每次随机 I/O 要付寻道 + 旋转延迟（毫秒级），所以小块随机写只有百级 IOPS；顺序写省掉寻道，吞吐达百 MB/s。按字节比，差距两个数量级以上，具体倍数取决于 I/O 块大小和盘型号。这正是 append-only / LSM 设计的出发点。
why_en: Each random I/O on a spinning disk pays seek plus rotational latency (milliseconds), so small random writes manage only hundreds of IOPS, while sequential writes skip the seek and reach hundreds of MB/s. By bytes the gap exceeds two orders of magnitude; the exact ratio depends on I/O size and drive model. This is why append-only and LSM designs exist.
options_en: Random I/O is about 100x faster than sequential, so the write path needs no special design
4 KB random writes reach ~100–200 IOPS (≈0.4–0.8 MB/s) while sequential writes reach ~100–200 MB/s — over two orders of magnitude apart by bytes
The gap is within 2x; seek latency is negligible
Disk I/O pattern has nothing to do with how a database designs its write path

termDefinitions.meaning: 固态硬盘，没有机械寻道臂，但顺序访问仍比随机访问更友好。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An SSD is flash-based storage with no mechanical seek arm, though sequential access is still friendlier than random access.

optionExplanations: 方向说反了——机械盘上顺序 I/O 才比随机快得多，不是随机比顺序快。
对：小块随机写受寻道和旋转延迟限制只有百级 IOPS（不到 1MB/s），顺序写能到百 MB/s，按字节差两个数量级以上，具体倍数取决于块大小和盘型号。
错：机械盘每次随机 I/O 都要付毫秒级寻道，差距远不止 2 倍，寻道延迟是主因。
磁盘 I/O 模式恰恰是很多存储引擎设计的出发点，append-only、LSM 这些结构都是为了适配它。
optionExplanations_en: That has it backwards — on spinning disks, sequential I/O is the one that's much faster than random.

Right: small random writes are limited by seek and rotational latency to hundreds of IOPS (under 1 MB/s), while sequential writes reach hundreds of MB/s — over two orders of magnitude by bytes; the exact ratio depends on I/O size and drive model.
Wrong: every random I/O on a spinning disk pays millisecond seeks, so the gap is far more than 2x and seek latency is the main cause.
I/O pattern is actually the starting point for a lot of storage-engine design — append-only and LSM structures exist specifically to work with it.

q: 把 LSM tree 写入路径按顺序排列：
q_en: Put the LSM tree write path in order:
steps: 后台 compaction 合并多个 SSTable，清理重复数据和 tombstone
新数据先写入内存中的有序 memtable
memtable 满后顺序刷盘成不可变的有序 SSTable
查询时可能需要检查 memtable 和多个磁盘文件
why: LSM 把前台随机写转为内存写和顺序刷盘，再把组织数据的成本放到后台 compaction。读取会承担检查多个文件的成本。
why_en: LSM trees write to a sorted memtable, flush immutable SSTables, compact them in the background, and may check multiple files on reads.
diagram:
flowchart LR
Write[Incoming points] --> Memtable[Sorted memtable]
Memtable --> SSTable[Immutable SSTable]
SSTable --> Compaction[Background compaction]
Compaction --> Larger[Large sorted files]
Query[Query] --> Memtable
Query --> SSTable

termDefinitions.meaning: 把随机写转成顺序写，再靠后台合并整理数据的存储结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An LSM tree turns random writes into sequential writes and reorganizes data later via background merges.

termDefinitions.meaning: LSM 刷盘后生成的不可变有序文件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An SSTable is the immutable sorted file an LSM tree writes when it flushes memory to disk.

termDefinitions.meaning: LSM 中驻留内存的有序缓冲结构，接收最新写入。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A memtable is the in-memory sorted buffer that absorbs the newest writes in an LSM tree.

termDefinitions.meaning: 合并多个存储文件、清理重复和已删除数据的后台过程。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Compaction is the background process that merges storage files and removes stale or deleted data.

termDefinitions.meaning: 标记某条数据已删除的占位记录，等 compaction 时才真正清除。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A tombstone is a marker recording that a value was deleted; it is physically removed only during compaction.

q: LSM（Log-Structured Merge Tree）的 memtable 为什么通常保持有序？
q_en: Why is the memtable in an LSM tree usually kept sorted?
options: 为了让每次写入都等磁盘完成排序之后才算成功返回
为了强制查询只能走全表顺序扫描，禁止建立或使用任何索引结构
为了把相邻 key 随机打散到不同文件，避免写热点
为了刷盘时直接产出有序 SSTable，方便范围扫描与合并
why: 内存里排序成本低，刷盘时直接顺序写出有序文件；有序文件支持二分查找、范围扫描，也让后台 merge-sort compaction 更高效。
why_en: A sorted memtable flushes into a sorted SSTable, enabling binary search, efficient ranges, and merge-based compaction.
options_en: So that every write only succeeds after the disk has finished sorting it.
So that queries are forced into full, sequential scans and can no longer build or use any index.
So that adjacent keys get scattered randomly across files to avoid write hotspots.
So the flush produces a sorted SSTable directly, which makes range scans and merges easy.

termDefinitions.meaning: LSM 中驻留内存的有序缓冲结构，接收最新写入。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A memtable is the in-memory sorted buffer that absorbs the newest writes in an LSM tree.

termDefinitions.meaning: LSM 刷盘后生成的不可变有序文件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An SSTable is the immutable sorted file an LSM tree writes when it flushes memory to disk.

optionExplanations: 内存里排序不等磁盘，写入确认在内存阶段就完成，不需要等磁盘排序好。
有序结构恰恰是为了支持二分查找等高效访问，不是用来禁用索引强制全表扫描的。
有序意味着按 key 顺序排列，不是打散分布；打散写入反而会破坏范围查询的局部性。
对，内存里已经排好序，刷盘后直接得到可以二分查找、范围扫描、方便合并的文件，不用额外再排一次。
optionExplanations_en: Sorting happens in memory, not on disk — a write can be acknowledged right there without waiting for any disk-side sort.
A sorted structure exists to enable efficient lookups like binary search — it does not force full scans or disable indexing.
Sorted means ordered by key, not scattered; scattering writes would actually break locality for range queries.
Right — because it's already ordered, flushing it to disk produces a file you can binary-search and merge without extra sorting work.
scenario: LSM 引擎每隔几分钟把 memtable 刷成一个 SSTable，而查询几乎都是按 series 的时间范围扫描。
scenario_en: The LSM engine flushes its memtable into an SSTable every few minutes, and queries are almost always range scans over one series.

q: LSM tree（日志结构合并树）的主要取舍是什么？
q_en: What is the main tradeoff of an LSM tree?
options: 牺牲所有写入能力，换取只读性能
前台写入变成顺序追加，代价是读可能要查多个 SSTable，以及 compaction 带来的后台写放大
牺牲压缩能力，换取更高空间占用
完全没有任何后台开销，因此性能只受磁盘限制
why: LSM 先写内存 + WAL，再整批顺序刷成 SSTable，前台写吞吐很高；代价是读可能要合并多个 SSTable（读放大），后台 compaction 要反复重写数据（写放大、短期空间放大）。它适合写多读少的指标流，不是所有 workload 的默认答案。
why_en: An LSM writes to memory plus a WAL and flushes sorted SSTables sequentially, so foreground write throughput is high; the cost is reads that may merge several SSTables (read amplification) and background compaction that rewrites data repeatedly (write amplification, temporary space amplification). It suits write-heavy metric streams, not every workload.
tradeoff: 高写入吞吐 vs 读放大与写放大
options_en: It gives up all write capability in exchange for read-only performance.
Foreground writes become sequential appends, at the cost of reads that may touch several SSTables plus background write amplification from compaction.
It gives up compression capability in exchange for higher space usage.
It has zero background overhead, so performance is limited only by disk.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把随机写转成顺序写，再靠后台合并整理数据的存储结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An LSM tree turns random writes into sequential writes and reorganizes data later via background merges.

termDefinitions.meaning: 由于 compaction 反复重写数据，实际磁盘写入量大于逻辑写入量的现象。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Write amplification means the actual bytes written to disk exceed the logical write size because compaction rewrites data multiple times.

optionExplanations: LSM 依然能高速写入，只是要接受一些读放大，说它牺牲全部写入能力是把代价夸大成了否定。
对，前台写入变成顺序追加，换来远高于原地更新的写入吞吐；代价是读放大，以及 compaction 带来的后台写放大。
LSM 通常反而借助压缩降低占用，这个选项把因果关系完全说反了。
后台 compaction 本身就是它的核心开销，说没有任何后台开销是忽略了它最大的代价来源。
optionExplanations_en: LSM trees still write fast — they just accept some read cost, so calling write capability "sacrificed entirely" overstates the tradeoff.
Right — foreground writes become sequential appends, giving far higher write throughput than in-place updates, at the cost of read amplification and background write amplification from compaction.
LSM engines typically use compression to cut space usage — this option has the causality backwards.
Background compaction is itself LSM's core overhead — claiming there's none ignores its biggest cost.
scenario: 监控写入 5 万点/秒，读取多是最近一小时的范围查询，团队在评估要不要上 LSM 引擎。
scenario_en: Monitoring takes 50k writes per second and most reads are last-hour range queries, and the team is weighing an LSM engine.

q: 补全 delta encoding 的思想：
q_en: Complete the idea behind delta encoding:
text: Delta encoding 不反复存完整值，而是存相邻值之间的 {{difference}}；时间序列相邻点通常变化小，所以这些 delta 更容易被 {{compressed}}。
why: CPU、内存、流量等指标通常连续且变化平滑，delta 值比原始值小。配合可变长编码能显著降低存储。
why_en: Delta encoding stores differences between adjacent values, which compress well when time-series data changes gradually.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  A["t1 t2 t3"] --> B["deltas"]
  B --> C["delta of delta"]
  C --> D["compressed block"]
codeSample:
Raw values:     45.2  45.3  45.1  45.4
Delta encoded:  45.2  +0.1  -0.2  +0.3
# 只存差值，差值比原值小很多，更容易压缩

termDefinitions.meaning: 存相邻值之间的差而不是完整值的编码方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Delta encoding stores the difference between adjacent values instead of the full value each time.

q: varint（variable-length encoding，变长整数编码）在 TSDB 压缩中解决什么问题？
q_en: What problem does varint, or variable-length encoding, solve in TSDB compression?
options: 把所有字符串自动转换成图片格式之后再落盘保存
强制每条记录都补齐到固定 1MB 大小之后再写入磁盘
让小整数只占 1-2 字节，而不是固定 4/8 字节
让浮点数从此无法用任何方式落盘保存
why: delta 往往是小数值，varint 能让小值占用 1-2 个字节。它放大了 delta encoding 的空间收益。
why_en: Variable-length encoding stores small deltas in fewer bytes instead of always using a fixed-width integer.
options_en: It converts every string into an image format before writing it to disk.
It pads every record out to a fixed 1MB size before writing it to disk.
It lets small integers take 1-2 bytes instead of a fixed 4 or 8.
It makes floating-point values impossible to persist at all.
codeSample:
varint(1)        = 0x01            (1 byte)
varint(300)      = 0xAC 0x02       (2 bytes)
varint(1000000)  = 0xC0 0x84 0x3D  (3 bytes)
# 值越小，占用字节越少；delta 编码后大多是小数值

termDefinitions.meaning: 变长整数编码，用更少字节表示小数值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Varint is a variable-length integer encoding that stores small numbers in fewer bytes.

optionExplanations: varint 处理的是整数编码，跟字符串转图片毫无关系，这是个无厘头选项。
varint 的意义正相反：它是变长的，小值用更少字节，不是强制补齐到固定大小。
对，小整数只占 1-2 字节而不是固定 4/8 字节，正好放大前面差值编码带来的空间收益。
varint 只管整数编码，浮点值有自己的压缩方式（比如 XOR），两者互不冲突。
optionExplanations_en: Varint is about integer encoding — turning strings into images has nothing to do with it.
Varint does the opposite — it's variable-length, using fewer bytes for small values, not padding everything to a fixed size.
Right — small integers take just 1-2 bytes instead of a fixed 4 or 8, which amplifies what delta encoding already saves.
Varint only handles integers — floats have their own compression path (like XOR), so the two do not conflict.
scenario: delta 编码后的指标差值多是个位数小整数，而 43 亿点/天的存储费是主要账单。
scenario_en: After delta encoding, most metric deltas are single-digit integers, and storage for 4.3 billion points a day is the main bill.

q: 时间戳 delta-of-delta（二阶差分）编码为什么对固定采样间隔特别有效？
q_en: Why is timestamp delta-of-delta encoding especially effective for fixed sampling intervals?
options: 因为 timestamp 不能被排序
因为相邻 timestamp 的间隔经常相同，二阶差分大量为 0
因为它会丢弃真实采样时间，只保留序号
因为所有 timestamp 都必须先转成字符串，再逐字符比较排序
why: 如果每 10 秒采样一次，timestamp 的 delta 基本恒定，delta-of-delta 接近 0。大量 0 非常容易压缩。
why_en: Delta-of-delta compression works well because regular sampling intervals make second-order timestamp deltas mostly zero.
options_en: Because timestamps cannot be sorted.
Because the interval between adjacent timestamps is often constant, so second-order deltas are mostly zero.
Because it discards the real sample time and keeps only a sequence number.
Because every timestamp must first be converted to a string and compared character by character.
codeSample:
Raw timestamps:   1000  1010  1020  1030  1040
Deltas:              10    10    10    10
Delta-of-delta:            0     0     0
# 间隔恒定 → 二阶差分几乎全 0 → 极易压缩

termDefinitions.meaning: 对增量再做一次差分的二阶编码，常用于规律采样的时间戳。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Delta-of-delta encoding takes the difference of deltas, which collapses to near zero for regularly spaced timestamps.

optionExplanations: timestamp 完全可以排序，这种二阶压缩生效的原因跟排序能力无关。
对，固定采样间隔下二阶差分几乎全是 0，0 值极容易压缩。
它照样保留真实采样时间，只是把相邻时间戳的差值再做一次差分，不是丢弃原始时间。
比较的是数值差，不需要先转字符串再逐字符比较，那样反而会拖慢压缩过程。
optionExplanations_en: Timestamps are perfectly sortable — that is not why delta-of-delta compression works well.
Right — with a fixed sampling interval, second-order deltas collapse to mostly zero, and zeros compress extremely well.
It still keeps the real sample times — it just takes a second difference of them, it does not discard the original timestamps.
The comparison is numeric — converting to strings and comparing character by character is not needed and would only slow the encoding down.
scenario: 每台机器固定每 10 秒采样一次，压缩前 timestamp 列就占掉很大一块空间。
scenario_en: Every host samples on a fixed 10-second interval, and before compression the timestamp column alone eats a big chunk of space.

q: TSDB 对浮点值常用 XOR 压缩的直觉是什么？
q_en: What is the intuition behind XOR compression for floating-point values in a TSDB?
options: 浮点数在时间序列里完全无法做任何形式的压缩处理
XOR 运算会把所有输入数值都折算成同一个固定常数输出
XOR 压缩只对文本字符串生效，对浮点数完全无效
相邻值接近时 XOR 后多数 bit 为 0，只存差异位
why: 相邻指标值通常很接近，二进制表示也有大量相同位。XOR 后只保留有意义的差异位，能显著减少空间。
why_en: XOR compression exploits similar adjacent floating-point values because their XOR contains many zero bits.
options_en: Floating-point values in time series simply cannot be compressed in any way.
XOR collapses every input value into one and the same fixed constant output.
XOR compression only works on text strings and does nothing for floats.
When neighboring values are close, most bits of their XOR are zero, so you store only the differing bits.

termDefinitions.meaning: 利用相邻浮点数按位异或后大量为 0 位来压缩数值的技术。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: XOR compression exploits the fact that XORing similar adjacent floating-point values leaves mostly zero bits.

optionExplanations: 浮点值同样能压缩，XOR 压缩正是专门针对时间序列里相邻浮点数设计的。
XOR 结果取决于两个输入的差异，值不同输出就不同，不会变成同一个固定常数。
XOR 压缩针对的是二进制位模式，浮点数的二进制表示同样适用，不是文本专属技巧。
对，相邻值接近时按位异或后前导位大多是 0，只存有意义的差异位就够了。
optionExplanations_en: Floats can absolutely be compressed — XOR compression was designed specifically for adjacent float values in time series.
XOR output depends on how the two inputs differ — different values give different results, not a single fixed constant.
XOR compression works on bit patterns, and a float's binary representation qualifies just as well — it is not text-only.
Right — when adjacent values are close, XORing them leaves mostly leading zeros, so only the differing bits need storing.
scenario: CPU 使用率相邻采样值往往只差零点几，但 43 亿点/天按 float64 原样存太贵。
scenario_en: Consecutive CPU-usage samples differ by only a fraction, yet storing 4.3 billion points a day as raw float64 is too expensive.

scenario: 监控系统每个点的有效信息只有 timestamp 和一个 float（约 16 字节），但落进普通行式表时，每一行还要带上 host、metric_name 等标签列，结果磁盘占用远超预期。
scenario_en: Each monitoring point's real information is just a timestamp and one float (about 16 bytes), but in a normal row-store table every row also carries label columns like host and metric_name, and disk usage grows far beyond expectation.
q: 为什么一条普通指标点的原始信息很小，但行式存储仍可能很浪费？
q_en: Why can a normal metric point be tiny in raw form but still waste space in row storage?
options: 因为每条指标都会被数据库自动复制成一段完整的视频文件长期保存
因为 timestamp + value 只有约 16 字节，每行却反复存 host、metric_name 和行头
因为 timestamp 这个字段本身在磁盘上要占用大约 10MB 空间
因为浮点数类型在关系数据库里天生完全无法进行任何压缩
why: 真正的数值部分只有约 16 字节，膨胀来自每行重复的标签字符串和行头（PostgreSQL 每行约 27 字节固定开销），再加索引条目。TSDB 按 series 存：标签只存一次，点只存压缩后的时间和值。
why_en: The actual payload is about 16 bytes; the bloat comes from label strings repeated on every row plus the per-row header (roughly 27 bytes of fixed overhead in PostgreSQL), plus index entries. A TSDB stores per series: labels once, then only compressed timestamps and values.
options_en: Because the database quietly copies every metric point into a full video file and keeps it around.
Because timestamp plus value is only about 16 bytes, while every row repeats host, metric_name, and a row header.
Because the timestamp field alone takes roughly 10MB of disk space.
Because float columns in a relational database inherently cannot be compressed at all.
optionExplanations: 数据库不会把指标点变成视频文件，这个选项纯属荒谬干扰项。
对，数值本身约 16 字节，真正膨胀的是每行反复重复的 host、metric_name 标签字符串和行头开销。
一个 timestamp 通常只占几字节，说它要占 10MB 完全不成立，是数量级错误。
浮点值同样可以压缩（比如 XOR 编码），说完全无法压缩不成立。
optionExplanations_en: A database does not turn metric points into video files — this is just a nonsense distractor.
Right — the value itself is about 16 bytes; what bloats is the host and metric_name label strings and row-header overhead repeated on every row.
A single timestamp is typically a few bytes — claiming it takes 10MB is off by many orders of magnitude.
Floating-point values can absolutely be compressed too (XOR encoding, for example) — "impossible to compress" does not hold up.

q: Time-based partitioning 在 TSDB 中的含义是什么？
q_en: What does time-based partitioning mean in a TSDB?
options: 按用户名哈希把数据随机拆成数量完全不受控的表
把所有历史数据永远放进一个不可删除的大文件里
按时间窗口切成不同 partition，比如按天或按周
只按 metric 数值大小分区，完全不看时间字段
why: 时间序列查询天然带时间范围，按时间窗口组织能让写入、读取和保留策略都更简单。不同 partition 可以在同机或多机上。
why_en: Time-based partitioning groups points into time-windowed chunks such as daily or weekly partitions.
diagram:
flowchart TD
  A["Time range"] --> B["Day partition"]
  A --> C["Week partition"]
  B --> D["Drop old partition"]
options_en: Hash on username to split data into an uncontrolled number of tables.
Keep all history forever inside one giant file that can never be deleted.
Slice data into partitions by time window, for example per day or per week.
Partition purely by the magnitude of the metric value, ignoring time.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按时间窗口（如按天/周）把数据切成不同 partition/chunk。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Time-based partitioning groups data into chunks by time window, such as daily or weekly.

optionExplanations: 这是按用户哈希分片的思路，跟按时间窗口组织数据是两件不同的事。
全放一个不可删除的大文件恰恰是时间分区想避免的，分区之后才能整段丢弃过期数据。
对，按天或按周这样的时间窗口切分数据，写入、查询、保留策略都能围绕它优化。
如果分区只看数值大小，同一时间点的数据可能散落各处，时间范围查询反而没法裁剪。
optionExplanations_en: That's user-hash sharding — a different idea entirely from organizing data by time window.
Dumping everything into one undeletable file is exactly what time partitioning avoids — partitions let you drop whole old chunks later.
Right — the data is chopped into time windows, say by day or by week, and everything else gets easier to reason about.
If partitioning only looked at the metric value, same-time data could scatter everywhere, and time-range queries would lose their ability to prune.
scenario: 监控数据只保留 30 天，查询几乎都带时间范围，引擎要决定按什么维度切分数据。
scenario_en: Metrics are kept for only 30 days and nearly every query carries a time range, so the engine must decide what dimension to split data on.

q: Time-based partitioning 带来哪些收益？
q_en: What benefits does time-based partitioning provide?
options: 所有高基数标签都会自动变低基数
新写入集中到当前时间 partition
保留策略可直接 drop 旧 partition
时间范围查询可以跳过不相关 partition
why: 按时间组织同时优化写入局部性、查询裁剪和数据过期。它不能解决 tag cardinality 爆炸。
why_en: Time partitions localize writes, prune reads by time range, and make retention as simple as dropping old partitions.
options_en: All high-cardinality tags automatically become low-cardinality.
New writes concentrate on the current time partition.
Retention can simply drop entire old partitions.
Time-range queries can skip irrelevant partitions.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按时间窗口（如按天/周）把数据切成不同 partition/chunk。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Time-based partitioning groups data into chunks by time window, such as daily or weekly.

optionExplanations: 分区不会改变标签基数，高基数 tag 该多还是多，这是两个不相关的问题。
对，新数据总是落在当前时间窗口，写入天然集中，局部性很好。
对，drop 掉整段旧 partition 比在巨表里逐行 DELETE 便宜得多。
对，查询能直接跳过时间范围之外的 partition，不用扫描无关数据。
optionExplanations_en: Partitioning does not change tag cardinality — a high-cardinality tag stays high-cardinality; the two are unrelated problems.
Right — new writes naturally land in the current time window, giving writes strong locality.
Right — dropping an entire old partition is far cheaper than deleting rows one by one from a giant table.
Right — queries can skip partitions entirely outside the requested time range instead of scanning them.
scenario: 指标保留 30 天、查询多为最近一小时，团队已按天分区，现在盘点实际拿到哪些收益。
scenario_en: With 30-day retention and mostly last-hour queries, the team already partitions by day and wants to know what that actually buys.

q: 为什么 TSDB 的保留策略通常比在巨表上 DELETE 旧行更便宜？
q_en: Why is TSDB retention usually cheaper than deleting old rows from a huge table?
options: 因为所有历史数据会在保留期到期后自动变成 0 字节但仍保留行
因为保留策略执行时完全不需要读取任何元数据
因为 TSDB 设计上永远不会删除任何数据
因为旧数据按时间分区存放，可直接删除整段旧文件
why: drop partition 是元数据/文件级操作，避免在巨表里扫描并删除海量旧行。监控数据常有明确生命周期，所以这个收益很大。
why_en: Retention is cheap because old time partitions can be dropped instead of deleting rows from a massive table.
options_en: Because all historical data automatically shrinks to 0 bytes at expiry but rows remain.
Because executing retention needs no metadata lookup at all.
Because a TSDB is designed to never delete any data.
Because old data lives in its own time partition, so retention can simply drop that entire file.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按时间窗口（如按天/周）把数据切成不同 partition/chunk。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Time-based partitioning groups data into chunks by time window, such as daily or weekly.

optionExplanations: 行还留着但变成 0 字节没有意义——保留策略的省钱方式是整段删除文件，不是把行清空。
执行保留策略仍然要查元数据才能定位该删哪个 partition，不是完全不看元数据。
TSDB 一样会删数据，只是删除的粒度是整个 partition 文件，而不是逐行删除。
对，旧数据独立成一个时间分区，保留窗口一到直接删这个文件就行，不用扫表。
optionExplanations_en: Rows staying around at zero bytes does not save anything — retention saves cost by dropping whole files, not hollowing out rows.
Executing retention still needs metadata lookups to find which partition to drop — it is not metadata-free.
A TSDB does delete data — just at the granularity of a whole partition file instead of row by row.
Right — old data lives in its own time partition, so once its window is up, retention just drops that file without scanning anything.
scenario: 43 亿点/天的表要每天清掉 30 天前的数据，同时不能拖慢在线写入。
scenario_en: A table taking 4.3 billion points a day must drop everything older than 30 days each night without slowing live writes.

q: 在这种数据模型中，tags 和 fields 最关键的区别是什么？

why_en: In an InfluxDB-style model, tags become part of the series key and are indexed, so they suit common filter dimensions; fields hold measured values, are not part of the series key and are not indexed, so they suit high-cardinality or store-only values without exploding the series count.
